discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable Rydberg-atom arrays for quantum simulation and quantum computing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Lukin proposed that the strong, long-range dipolar interaction between Rydberg atoms creates a 'blockade' that forbids double excitation within micrometres. This turns neutral atoms into a platform for fast entangling gates and collective quantum states. Browaeys and Lukin then realised it experimentally. They demonstrated blockade between two single atoms, assembled defect-free arrays of hundreds of atoms in optical tweezers, and used them to observe quantum phase transitions, quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquids. Recently they implemented error-detected logical qubits. This work created a new subfield in which interactions between atoms, rather than between atoms and light, are engineered with full control. It links atomic physics, condensed-matter many-body theory and quantum information. Today Rydberg arrays are among the leading routes to scalable quantum simulators and computers.
